positions.name: SignedManifestGateJustification
positions.frame: what past incident is being invoked to justify making a signed release manifest mandatory for Meridian deploys?
positions.why: Quinton's directive imposing the signed-manifest requirement and his causal claim about two unsigned artifacts reaching staging last quarter read as one directional move: the mandate is not asserted as abstract policy but as a proportionate, incident-driven response. The pairing holds the mandate (decision-grade, authority-ranking) and its rational-persuasion justification together — the second segment supplies the 'why' the first segment doesn't argue for on its own.

positions.name: MeridianGateDecisionRecord
positions.frame: what are the codified terms — requirement, environmental scope, and ownership — of the Meridian deployment gate as recorded in the decision?
positions.why: Xena's three bolded label-colon-value lines (Gate, Scope, Owner) share footing (animator=author=Xena, no principal), the same compressed jargon-native register, and the same stock label-value formatting convention. Read together they specify one thing: the settled terms of the gate as documented — not Quinton's own justificatory speech, but the record derived from it, spanning the rule itself, its reach across staging and production, and the accountable owner.
